verses.sloka: उषित्वा रजनीम् तत्र राजपुत्रावरिम्दमौ ।महर्षिमभिवाद्याथ जग्मतुस्तम् गिरिम् प्रति ॥२-५५-१॥
verses.transliteration: uṣitvā rajanīm tatra rājaputrāvarimdamau ।maharṣimabhivādyātha jagmatustam girim prati ॥2-55-1॥

translations.english: After spending the night, the princes, destroyers of enemies, offered obeisance to that great sage (Bharadhwaja) and went towards that mount Chitrkuta.
translations.hindi: „ 2 ६ हति िपछाशःसगः॥।- 7 > ५४ I . तद्चन्तर उन महाबली रघुबंशबद्धेन दोनों भाइयों ने, उस , निजेन बन में भय और उद्वेग वर्जित हो, वैसे ही बास किया, _ जैसे पर्वतशिखर पर रहने वाले दो सिंह निभेय हो, बास करते ` ` योऽ + > a Pare PEST “३०२१ एवमेतत्पुरावृत्तमाख्यानं भद्रमस्तु बः। प्रवयाहरत विस्रब्धं बलं विष्णोः प्रवधताम्‌

verses.sloka: तेषाम् चैव स्वस्त्ययनम् महर्षिः स चकार ह ।प्रस्थिताम्श्चैव तान् प्रेक्ष्यपिता पुत्रानिवान्वगात् ॥२-५५-२॥
verses.transliteration: teṣām caiva svastyayanam maharṣiḥ sa cakāra ha ।prasthitāmścaiva tān prekṣyapitā putrānivānvagāt ॥2-55-2॥

translations.english: Seeing them setting forth, the great sage blessed them for a safe journey and followed them like a father following his children.

verses.sloka: ततः प्रचक्रमे वक्तुम् वचनम् स महामुनिः ।भर्द्वाजो महातेजा रामम् सत्यपराक्रमम् ॥२-५५-३॥
verses.transliteration: tataḥ pracakrame vaktum vacanam sa mahāmuniḥ ।bhardvājo mahātejā rāmam satyaparākramam ॥2-55-3॥

translations.english: Then that great effulgent sage Bharadwaja began to speak to Rama whose strength was truth.

verses.sloka: गङ्गायमुनयोः सन्धिमासाद्य मनुजर्षभौ ।काLइन्दीमनुगच्छेताम् नदीम् पश्चान्मुखाश्रिताम् ॥२-५५-४॥
verses.transliteration: gaṅgāyamunayoḥ sandhimāsādya manujarṣabhau ।kāLindīmanugacchetām nadīm paścānmukhāśritām ॥2-55-4॥

translations.english: Reaching the confluence of rivers Ganga and Yamuna, O Rama and Lakshmana best among men proceed along the Kalindi (Yamuna) river flowing westward.

verses.sloka: अथासाद्य तु काLइन्न्धीम् शीघ्रस्रोतसमापगाम् ।तस्यास्तीर्थम् प्रचरितम् पुराणम् प्रेक्ष्य राघवौ ॥२-५५-५॥
verses.transliteration: athāsādya tu kāLinndhīm śīghrasrotasamāpagām ।tasyāstīrtham pracaritam purāṇam prekṣya rāghavau ॥2-55-5॥

translations.english: On reaching that swiftflowing river Yamuna, O Rama and Lakshmana O scions of the Raghu race, you will find an ancient spot (on the river bank). There make a raft and cross Kalindi, daughter of the Sun.

verses.sloka: तत्र यूयम् प्लवम् कृत्वा तरताम्शुमतीम् नदीम् ।ततो न्यग्रोधमासाद्य महान्तम् हरितच्छदम् ॥२-५५-६॥
verses.transliteration: tatra yūyam plavam kṛtvā taratāmśumatīm nadīm ।tato nyagrodhamāsādya mahāntam haritacchadam ॥2-55-6॥

translations.english: There you will find a large, banyan tree with its lush green leaves, looking dark with its densely grown trees. It is inhabited by siddhas. Sita should offer with folded palms invocations for her wellbeing.

verses.sloka: विवृद्धम् बहुभिर्वऋक्षैह् श्यामम् सिद्धोपसेवितम् ।तस्मै सीताञ्जलिम् कृत्वा प्रयुञ्जीताशिषः शिवाः ॥२-५५-७॥
verses.transliteration: vivṛddham bahubhirvaṛkṣaih śyāmam siddhopasevitam ।tasmai sītāñjalim kṛtvā prayuñjītāśiṣaḥ śivāḥ ॥2-55-7॥

translations.english: There you will find a large, banyan tree with its lush green leaves, looking dark with its densely grown trees. It is inhabited by siddhas. Sita should offer with folded palms invocations for her wellbeing.

verses.sloka: समासाद्य तु तम् वृक्षम् वसेद्वातिक्रमेत वा ।क्रोशमात्रम् ततो गत्वा नीलम् द्रक्ष्यथ काननम् ॥२-५५-८॥
verses.transliteration: samāsādya tu tam vṛkṣam vasedvātikrameta vā ।krośamātram tato gatvā nīlam drakṣyatha kānanam ॥2-55-8॥

translations.english: Reaching that tree, you may tarry or proceed further. A krosa from there, you will see a beautiful forest filled with dark trees mixed with Palasas and badaris and bamboos on the Yamuna.

verses.sloka: पलाशबदरीमिश्रम् रम्यम् वम्शैश्च यामुनैः ।स पन्थाश्चित्रकूटस्य गतः सुबहुशो मया ॥२-५५-९॥
verses.transliteration: palāśabadarīmiśram ramyam vamśaiśca yāmunaiḥ ।sa panthāścitrakūṭasya gataḥ subahuśo mayā ॥2-55-9॥

translations.english: That path leads to Chitrakuta. I had travelled through it several times. It is beautiful, smooth and safe from forest fires.

verses.sloka: रम्ये मार्दवयुक्तश्च वनदावैर्विपर्जितः ।इति पन्थानमावेद्य महर्षः स न्यवर्तत ॥२-५५-१०॥
verses.transliteration: ramye mārdavayuktaśca vanadāvairviparjitaḥ ।iti panthānamāvedya maharṣaḥ sa nyavartata ॥2-55-10॥

translations.english: The great sage returned after instructing Rama about the path. So be it, said Rama and offering obeisance requested Bharadhwaja to go back.
translations.hindi: वेदवेये परे पुंसि जाते दशरथात्मज । वेदः प्राचेतसादासीत्साक्षाद्रामायंणात्मना

verses.sloka: अभिवाद्य तथेत्युक्त्वा रामेण विनिवर्तितः ।उपावृत्ते मुनौ तस्मिन् रामो लक्ष्मणमब्रवीत् ॥२-५५-११॥
verses.transliteration: abhivādya tathetyuktvā rāmeṇa vinivartitaḥ ।upāvṛtte munau tasmin rāmo lakṣmaṇamabravīt ॥2-55-11॥

translations.english: With the sage gone, Rama said, O Saumitri (son of Sumitra) we are lucky, for the sage has been so kind.

verses.sloka: कृतपुण्याः स्म सौमित्रे मुनिर्यन्नोऽनुकम्पते ।इति तौ पुरुषव्याघ्रौ मन्त्रयित्वा मनस्विनौ ॥२-५५-१२॥
verses.transliteration: kṛtapuṇyāḥ sma saumitre muniryanno'nukampate ।iti tau puruṣavyāghrau mantrayitvā manasvinau ॥2-55-12॥

translations.english: Thus talking with one another, the two nobleminded tigers (best) among men advanced towards river Kalindi (Yamuna) with Sita walking in front.

verses.sloka: सीतामेवाग्रतः कृत्वा काLइन्दीम् जग्मतुर्नदीम् ।अथा साद्य तु काLइन्दीम् शीघ्रस्रोतोवहाम् नदीम् ॥२-५५-१३॥
verses.transliteration: sītāmevāgrataḥ kṛtvā kāLindīm jagmaturnadīm ।athā sādya tu kāLindīm śīghrasrotovahām nadīm ॥2-55-13॥

translations.english: Thereafter, they all reached the rapidly flowing river Kalindi and began pondering how to cross it.

verses.sloka: तौ काष्ठसम्घातमथो चक्रतुस्तु महाप्लवम् ॥२-५५-१४॥
verses.transliteration: tau kāṣṭhasamghātamatho cakratustu mahāplavam ॥2-55-14॥

translations.english: Then they both made a big wooden float by joining logs of wood, spreading bamboos on it and covering it with the (fragrant roots of) Ushira bushes.

verses.sloka: शुष्कैर्वम्शैः समास्तीर्णमुLईरैश्च समावृतम् ।ततो वेतसशाखाश्च जम्बूशाखाश्च वीर्यवान् ॥२-५५-१५॥
verses.transliteration: śuṣkairvamśaiḥ samāstīrṇamuLīraiśca samāvṛtam ।tato vetasaśākhāśca jambūśākhāśca vīryavān ॥2-55-15॥

translations.english: The valiant Lakshmana cut the stems of reeds and branches of the Jambu tree to prepare a comfortable seat for Sita (on that float).

verses.sloka: चकार लक्ष्मणश्छित्वा सीतायाः सुखमासनम् ।तत्र श्रियमिवाचिन्त्याम् रामो दाशरथिः प्रियाम् ॥२-५५-१६॥
verses.transliteration: cakāra lakṣmaṇaśchitvā sītāyāḥ sukhamāsanam ।tatra śriyamivācintyām rāmo dāśarathiḥ priyām ॥2-55-16॥

translations.english: Rama, son of Dasaratha helped his beloved (Sita), who was looking inconceivably like Lakshmi (goddess of wealth) and was feeling a little bashful while stepping on to the float.
translations.hindi: वेदवेद्ये परे पु'सि जाते दशरथात्मजे । वेदः प्राचेतसादा पीत्साक्षाद्रामाय णात्मना

verses.sloka: ईष्त्सन्कह्हनाबान् तानग्तारिओअतत् प्लवम् ।पार्श्वे च तत्र वैदेह्या वसने चूष्णानि च ॥२-५५-१७॥
verses.transliteration: īṣtsankahhanābān tānagtārioatat plavam ।pārśve ca tatra vaidehyā vasane cūṣṇāni ca ॥2-55-17॥

translations.english: Rama placed robes and ornaments on the float by the side of Sita and a spade and a basket along with weapons.
translations.hindi: वेदवेद्ये परे पुंसि जाते दशरथात्मजे । वेदः प्राचेतसादासीत्साक्षाद्रामायणात्मना

verses.sloka: प्लवे कठिनकाजम् च रामश्चक्रे सहायुधैः ।आरोप्य प्रथमम् सीताम् सम्घाटम् प्रतिगृह्य तौ ॥२-५५-१८॥
verses.transliteration: plave kaṭhinakājam ca rāmaścakre sahāyudhaiḥ ।āropya prathamam sītām samghāṭam pratigṛhya tau ॥2-55-18॥

translations.english: Those valiant sons of Dasaratha held the float (firmly) to help Sita step on to it. Then they crossed the river carefully.

verses.sloka: ततः प्रतेरतुर्य त्तौ वीरौ दशरथात्मजौ ।काLइन्दीमध्यमायाता सीता त्वेनामवन्दत ॥२-५५-१९॥
verses.transliteration: tataḥ prateraturya ttau vīrau daśarathātmajau ।kāLindīmadhyamāyātā sītā tvenāmavandata ॥2-55-19॥

translations.english: On reaching the middle of the river Yamuna, Sita made reverential salutations to her saying O goddess, I am crossing you, may safety be ours and may my husband fulfil his vow After Rama's (safe) return to the city (of Ayodhya) ruled by the Ikshvaku kings, I shall worship you with a thousand cows and a hundred pots of wine.

verses.sloka: स्वस्ति देवि तरामि त्वाम् पार्येन्मे पतिर्वतम् ।यक्ष्ये त्वाम् गोनहस्रेण सुराघटशतेन च ॥२-५५-२०॥
verses.transliteration: svasti devi tarāmi tvām pāryenme patirvatam ।yakṣye tvām gonahasreṇa surāghaṭaśatena ca ॥2-55-20॥

translations.english: On reaching the middle of the river Yamuna, Sita made reverential salutations to her saying O goddess, I am crossing you, may safety be ours and may my husband fulfil his vow After Rama's (safe) return to the city (of Ayodhya) ruled by the Ikshvaku kings, I shall worship you with a thousand cows and a hundred pots of wine.

verses.sloka: स्वस्ति प्रत्यागते रामे पुरीमिक्ष्वाकुपालिताम् ।काLइन्दीमथ सीता तु याचमाना कृताञ्जलिः ॥२-५५-२१॥
verses.transliteration: svasti pratyāgate rāme purīmikṣvākupālitām ।kāLindīmatha sītā tu yācamānā kṛtāñjaliḥ ॥2-55-21॥

translations.english: While Sita with her fair complexion was thus invoking river Yamuna with folded hands they reached the southern bank.

verses.sloka: तीरमेवाभिसम्प्राप्ता दक्षिणम् वरवर्णिनी ।ततः प्लवेनाम्शुमतीम् शीघ्रगामूर्मिमालिनीम् ॥२-५५-२२॥
verses.transliteration: tīramevābhisamprāptā dakṣiṇam varavarṇinī ।tataḥ plavenāmśumatīm śīghragāmūrmimālinīm ॥2-55-22॥

translations.english: They crossed the swiftflowing river Yamuna, daughter of the Sungod, full of waves and with trees growing thick on her banks.

verses.sloka: तीरजैर्बहुभिर्वृक्षैः सम्तेरुर्यमुनाम् नदीम् ।ते तीर्णाः प्लवमुत्सृज्य प्रस्थाय यमुनावनात् ॥२-५५-२३॥
verses.transliteration: tīrajairbahubhirvṛkṣaiḥ samteruryamunām nadīm ।te tīrṇāḥ plavamutsṛjya prasthāya yamunāvanāt ॥2-55-23॥

translations.english: Having crossed the river, they left the float and proceeded from the adjoining forest of Yamuna and reached the dark, cool banyan tree covered with lush green leaves.

verses.sloka: श्यामम् न्यग्रोधमासेदुः शीतलम् हरितच्छदम् ।न्य्ग्रोधम् तमुपागम्य वैदेहि वाक्यमब्रवीत् ॥२-५५-२४॥
verses.transliteration: śyāmam nyagrodhamāseduḥ śītalam haritacchadam ।nygrodham tamupāgamya vaidehi vākyamabravīt ॥2-55-24॥

translations.english: Having reached the banyan tree, Sita invoked it, saying, 'O great tree I offer you my salutations. May my husband fulfil his vow May I behold Kausalya and the illustrious Sumitra on my return. Saying so, she went round the tree offering reverential salutations with folded hands.

verses.sloka: नमस्तेऽन्तु महावृक्ष पारयेन्मे पतिर्वतम् ।कौसल्याम् चैव पश्येयम् सुमित्राम् च यशस्विनीम् ॥२-५५-२५॥
verses.transliteration: namaste'ntu mahāvṛkṣa pārayenme patirvatam ।kausalyām caiva paśyeyam sumitrām ca yaśasvinīm ॥2-55-25॥

translations.english: Having reached the banyan tree, Sita invoked it, saying, 'O great tree I offer you my salutations. May my husband fulfil his vow May I behold Kausalya and the illustrious Sumitra on my return. Saying so, she went round the tree offering reverential salutations with folded hands.

verses.sloka: इति सीताञ्जलिम् कृत्वा पर्यगच्छद्वनस्पतिम् ।अवलोक्य ततः सीतामायाचन्तीमनिन्दिताम् ॥२-५५-२६॥
verses.transliteration: iti sītāñjalim kṛtvā paryagacchadvanaspatim ।avalokya tataḥ sītāmāyācantīmaninditām ॥2-55-26॥

translations.english: Beholding the obedient, blemishless, beloved Sita invoking blessings, Rama said to Lakhsmana:

verses.sloka: दयिताम् च विधेयम् च रामो लक्ष्मणमब्रवीत् ।सीतामादाय गच्छ त्वमग्रतो भरतानुज ॥२-५५-२७॥
verses.transliteration: dayitām ca vidheyam ca rāmo lakṣmaṇamabravīt ।sītāmādāya gaccha tvamagrato bharatānuja ॥2-55-27॥

translations.english: O Lakshmana, best among bipeds (men) and brother of Bharata walk ahead with Sita and I shall follow with weapons.

verses.sloka: पृष्ठतोऽहम् गमिष्यामि सायुधो द्विपदाम् वर ।यद्यत्फलम् प्रार्थयते पुष्पम् वा जनकात्मजा ॥२-५५-२८॥
verses.transliteration: pṛṣṭhato'ham gamiṣyāmi sāyudho dvipadām vara ।yadyatphalam prārthayate puṣpam vā janakātmajā ॥2-55-28॥

translations.english: Whatever fruit or flower the daughter of Janaka asks for, get it. Whatever pleases her mind give it.

verses.sloka: तत्तत्प्रदद्या वैदेह्या यत्रास्य रमते मनः ।गच्चतोस्तु तयोर्मध्ये बभूव जनकात्मजा ॥२-५५-२९॥
verses.transliteration: tattatpradadyā vaidehyā yatrāsya ramate manaḥ ।gaccatostu tayormadhye babhūva janakātmajā ॥2-55-29॥

translations.english: The daughter of Janaka walked between them like a sheelephant between two males.

verses.sloka: मातङ्गयोर्मद्यगता शुभा नागवधूरिव ।एकैकम् पादपम् गुल्मम् लताम् वा पुष्पशालिनीम् ॥२-५५-३०॥
verses.transliteration: mātaṅgayormadyagatā śubhā nāgavadhūriva ।ekaikam pādapam gulmam latām vā puṣpaśālinīm ॥2-55-30॥

translations.english: That gentle lady enquired of Rama about a tree or a shrub or a creeper in full bloom which she did not see before.

verses.sloka: अदृष्टपूर्वाम् पश्यन्ती रामम् पप्रच्छ साऽबला ।रमणीयान् बहुविधान् पादपान् कुसुमोत्कटान् ॥२-५५-३१॥
verses.transliteration: adṛṣṭapūrvām paśyantī rāmam papraccha sā'balā ।ramaṇīyān bahuvidhān pādapān kusumotkaṭān ॥2-55-31॥

translations.english: Cheered by Sita's indents, Lakshmana brought her various beautiful plants and stocks of flowers.

verses.sloka: सीतावचनसम्रब्द अनयामास लक्स्मणः ।विचित्रवालुकजलाम् हससारसनादिताम् ॥२-५५-३२॥
verses.transliteration: sītāvacanasamrabda anayāmāsa laksmaṇaḥ ।vicitravālukajalām hasasārasanāditām ॥2-55-32॥

translations.english: Beholding the river Yamuna with its wonderful water and sand echoing with the cackle of swans and cranes, Sita went ecstatic.

verses.sloka: रेमे जनकराजस्य तदा प्रेक्ष्य सुता नदीम् ।क्रोशमात्रम् ततो गत्वा भ्रातरौ रामलक्ष्मनौ ॥२-५५-३३॥
verses.transliteration: reme janakarājasya tadā prekṣya sutā nadīm ।krośamātram tato gatvā bhrātarau rāmalakṣmanau ॥2-55-33॥

translations.english: After walking a krosa into the forest on the bank of Yamuna, the two brothers killed many deer suitable for sacrifice and ate them.

verses.sloka: बहून्मेध्यान् मृगान् हत्वा चेरतुर्यमुनावने ।विहृत्य ते बर्हिणपूगनादिते ।शुभे वने वानरवारणायुते ।समम् नदीवप्रमुपेत्य सम्मतम् ।निवासमाजग्मु रदीनदर्शनाः ॥२-५५-३४॥
verses.transliteration: bahūnmedhyān mṛgān hatvā ceraturyamunāvane ।vihṛtya te barhiṇapūganādite ।śubhe vane vānaravāraṇāyute ।samam nadīvapramupetya sammatam ।nivāsamājagmu radīnadarśanāḥ ॥2-55-34॥

translations.english: They reached the tableland on the bank of that river and moved in high spirit in the lovely forest resounding with cries of flocks of peacocks and teeming with monkeys and elephants. Finally they selected a spot for their stay. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे पञ्चपञ्चाशस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the fiftyfifth sarga in Ayodhyakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.
